intro: On 20 November 2026, SIAM held its first National EV Charging Day in New Delhi, with support from the Ministry of Heavy Industries. Participants discussed charging reliability, access, maintenance and the coordination needed for a scalable Indian EV charging network.
The event is a useful prompt to examine customer-facing charging readiness. It does not establish the number of operational chargers, local availability or a new binding dealership requirement.

interpretation.heading: Make the charging promise verifiable
points: Confirm connector compatibility, access hours, payment method and latest known availability before sharing a charging location.
Test the dealership's approved charging equipment through qualified personnel and record failed sessions, corrective actions and restoration times.
Review actual demand and total ownership cost before investing in additional charging capacity.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Verify the charging handover
desks.check: Confirm home or workplace charging plan, compatible public alternatives and escalation contact at EV delivery.
desks.metric: EV deliveries with documented charging briefing ÷ EV deliveries reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: A customer needs a usable plan, not just a map pin.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Track charger availability
desks.check: Use authorised staff to log scheduled charger service hours and unavailable hours; escalate faults to the approved provider.
desks.metric: Available charger-hours ÷ scheduled charger-hours (%)
desks.rationale: Installed equipment is not necessarily usable.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Verify charging accessories
desks.check: Check approved compatibility, stock and supplier ETA for promised cables and accessories.
desks.metric: Verified accessory lines ÷ promised accessory lines reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: Incorrect accessories can delay safe handover.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Check charging evidence before valuation
desks.check: Record supplied cable, connector condition and authorised functional test evidence before EV appraisal approval.
desks.metric: EV appraisals with complete charging evidence ÷ EV appraisals reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: Unverified charging condition creates resale and repair risk.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Measure charging cost
desks.check: Reconcile charger meter readings, electricity expense and completed sessions for the same monthly period and boundary.
desks.metric: Allocated charging electricity expense (₹) ÷ completed charging sessions (₹/session)
desks.rationale: Electricity cost per session is not total charger operating cost.

issues.huddleTitle: One EV delivery. One charging readiness check.
issues.huddleSummary: Use an actual upcoming EV delivery or a documented case if none is due. End with a Ready/Hold decision, accountable owner, deadline and customer update.
huddle: 0–3 min: SALES checks the customer's charging plan and alternatives.
3–6 min: SERVICE reviews charger availability logs and escalation route.
6–9 min: SPARES confirms approved cable and accessory availability.
9–12 min: USED CARS reviews charging-condition evidence if an exchange applies; otherwise reviews a sample EV appraisal.
12–15 min: ACCOUNTS checks charging-cost records; agree decision, owner and deadline.
limitations: The source is an event report, not evidence of operational charger counts, reliability, national penetration or financial returns. Numerical claims from speeches are omitted because their underlying datasets or denominators were not independently verified.

Full indexed SIAM primary release and official photo gallery agree on the event date; direct retrieval of the release and event page timed out. Live URL verification is pending; status remains draft and publication is withheld.
KPIs are RPHV recommendations, not SIAM mandates. Use the same period and scope for numerator and denominator; zero denominators are N/A. No physical electrical testing is part of the huddle.

issues.title: Festive retail set a record. Passenger vehicles tell a different story.
issues.summary: FADA's 42-day festive registration data show a growing overall market but fewer passenger vehicles than last festive season. Electric passenger-vehicle registrations rose sharply. Dealers should reconcile their own demand by model and powertrain before placing fresh orders.
issues.sourceNote: FADA release dated 23 November 2026, compiled 22 November; festive 2026: 11 October–21 November; festive 2025: 22 September–2 November. Both windows are 42 days, not calendar months.

metrics.label: All-category retail registrations
metrics.context: +2.21% versus festive 2025

issues.reportingType: Registration-based retail snapshot from FADA/MoRTH; not OEM wholesales, bookings, a survey or final revised data.
intro: FADA's 23 November release records 55,25,490 registrations across six vehicle categories, compared with 54,05,956 in the equivalent 2025 festive window. Passenger vehicles fell from 8,06,322 to 7,48,616, while electric passenger vehicles rose from 30,133 to 52,104.

Electric passenger vehicles accounted for approximately 6.96% of reported PV registrations this festive period versus 3.74% last year (RPHV calculation: electric PV registrations divided by all PV registrations in each window). These are national reported aggregates, not a forecast for a particular outlet.

interpretation.heading: Plan December by model and powertrain
points: Separate live bookings, confirmed VIN allocations and registrations in the local demand review.
Review lost enquiries and cancellation reasons before changing the stock mix; do not infer local EV demand from national growth alone.
Align workshop skill coverage, parts replenishment and inventory funding with verified demand.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Audit the live order book
desks.check: Reconfirm model, powertrain, delivery date and customer intent for each active booking; exclude cancelled orders.
desks.metric: Reconfirmed active bookings ÷ active bookings reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: An aggregate market record does not clear an individual dealer's stock.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Check powertrain readiness
desks.check: Match next week's scheduled jobs to trained technicians and approved diagnostic equipment.
desks.metric: Scheduled jobs with verified skill and tool coverage ÷ scheduled jobs reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: A changing vehicle mix changes aftersales requirements.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Replenish against actual demand
desks.check: Compare proposed purchase lines with recent consumption, reservations, VIN fitment and supplier lead times.
desks.metric: Purchase lines supported by documented demand ÷ proposed purchase lines reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: National registration growth does not justify every local reorder.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Refresh exchange valuations
desks.check: Check local comparable resale evidence, inspection cost and ownership documents before approving an exchange.
desks.metric: Exchange appraisals with current evidence ÷ appraisals reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: A market-level trend is not a vehicle-specific valuation.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Fund confirmed demand first
desks.check: Review unallocated stock by age, cost and finance exposure before approving new orders.
desks.metric: Funded unallocated vehicle stock at 60+ days (₹ at acquisition cost)
desks.rationale: A profitable mix must also be affordable to hold.

issues.huddleTitle: One model. One demand-to-stock decision.
issues.huddleSummary: Select a model with excess stock or an allocation shortage. End with an order, transfer or hold decision, named owner and review deadline.
huddle: 0–3 min: SALES verifies active orders and lost-enquiry reasons.
3–6 min: SERVICE checks skill and tool readiness for the selected powertrain.
6–9 min: SPARES checks demand, fitment and supplier lead time.
9–12 min: USED CARS checks exchange valuation and refurbishment exposure.
12–15 min: ACCOUNTS checks stock funding; agree action, owner and deadline.
limitations: FADA compiled the snapshot on 22 November 2026 from 1,468 of 1,469 RTOs. Telangana registrations for three-wheelers, commercial vehicles and tractors were unavailable for festive 2026. Later revisions are possible; coverage may differ between years.

The overall total includes two-wheelers, three-wheelers, commercial vehicles, wheeled construction equipment, passenger vehicles and tractors. Electric PV share uses only the PV denominator, not all vehicles. Growth is against the corresponding festive 2025 window, not October 2025 or a monthly comparison.

The release uses equal 42-day festival-relative windows, allowing for registration lag. No causal attribution, local forecast, wholesale comparison or dealer profitability claim is made. KPIs and 60-day threshold are RPHV suggestions; zero denominators are not applicable.

issues.title: Turnover is not profit. Profit is not cash.
issues.summary: Popular Vehicles and Services reported quarterly revenue from operations of ₹2,088.92 crore and profit after tax of ₹2.20 crore. Its separate half-year cash-flow statement records a net operating cash outflow of ₹178.66 crore. RPHV recommends a daily review of contribution, ageing and collections.
issues.sourceNote: Popular Vehicles and Services Limited consolidated Ind AS exchange filing, 11 November 2026. Q2 FY27: 1 July–30 September 2026; H1 cash flow: 1 April–30 September 2026. Unaudited, subject to statutory auditor limited review.

issues.reportingType: Unaudited consolidated company financial results; not manufacturer wholesales, customer registrations or survey data.
intro: In its 11 November 2026 exchange filing, Indian dealership group Popular Vehicles and Services Limited reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹2,088.92 crore, finance costs of ₹32.01 crore and profit after tax of ₹2.20 crore.

For the separate six-month period ended 30 September, the group reported net cash used in operating activities of ₹178.66 crore, despite positive half-year profit after tax of ₹3.57 crore. The cash-flow reconciliation includes an inventory increase adjustment of ₹302.27 crore. These are group financial figures, not vehicle counts.

RPHV interpretation: a dealership needs three distinct views—sales contribution, accounting profit and actual cash movement. Review stock funding and outstanding collections before committing more capital. The filing does not establish that one particular department caused the cash outflow.

interpretation.heading: Close the loop from invoice to cash
points: Review actual gross contribution per vehicle after approved discounts and direct deal costs; keep accounting profit separate.
Assign aged stock and outstanding receivables a named owner, expected recovery date and next action.
Maintain a rolling weekly cash forecast showing confirmed receipts, unavoidable payments and borrowing headroom.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Check contribution before delivery
desks.check: Review the deal sheet for selling price, vehicle cost, discounts and direct deal costs before release.
desks.metric: Delivered deals with approved contribution sheet ÷ delivered deals reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: Sales volume alone cannot establish margin.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Convert completed work into invoices
desks.check: Review ready-for-delivery repair orders that have not been invoiced; verify approval and billing status.
desks.metric: Completed ROs unbilled for more than 24 hours (count)
desks.rationale: Completed work is not necessarily billed or collected.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Release capital from slow-moving inventory
desks.check: Review items without movement for 90 days and confirm return, transfer or genuine demand before reordering.
desks.metric: Value of stock without movement for 90+ days ÷ total parts stock value (%)
desks.rationale: Inventory consumes working capital until sold or otherwise recovered.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Measure holding cost before buying
desks.check: Approve purchase, refurbishment, estimated holding cost and realistic net resale proceeds for each proposed acquisition.
desks.metric: Acquisitions with approved full-cost appraisal ÷ acquisitions reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: An apparent trading margin can disappear while stock is held.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Build a seven-day cash forecast
desks.check: Reconcile bank balances, confirmed receipts, supplier dues, payroll and finance obligations; flag any funding gap.
desks.metric: Lowest projected closing cash balance over the next 7 days (₹)
desks.rationale: A positive profit does not guarantee funds for upcoming payments.

issues.huddleTitle: Trace one transaction from margin to money.
issues.huddleSummary: Choose a real delivered vehicle or completed repair with money still outstanding. End with a recovery action, named owner, deadline and updated cash forecast.
huddle: 0–3 min: SALES checks the approved deal contribution and promised settlement.
3–6 min: SERVICE verifies completion, billing or pending authorisation.
6–9 min: SPARES confirms parts issue and associated direct costs.
9–12 min: USED CARS checks any exchange settlement and holding cost, or identifies a comparable stock exception.
12–15 min: ACCOUNTS reconciles receipts and commitments; assign owner, recovery deadline and next review.
limitations: The figures are consolidated results of one Indian dealership group, not national totals or individual outlet benchmarks. The filing covers the parent and applicable subsidiaries; the group composition changed across reporting periods. No year-on-year comparison is made.

Q2 revenue, finance cost and PAT cover July–September 2026; net operating cash flow, inventory adjustment and half-year PAT cover April–September 2026. Do not subtract the six-month cash flow from quarterly profit.

The original filing reports INR lakhs. Divide by 100 for crore and round to two decimals: 208892.10, 3200.50, 220.40, −17865.70, 30226.70 and 357.00 lakh respectively. Finance costs are not assumed to be solely inventory interest.

Unaudited interim results received statutory auditor limited review. The data do not establish a single cause of cash outflow, nor any individual dealership performance. All checks and KPIs are RPHV recommendations. Zero denominators are not applicable.

issues.title: Four service bays. How much vehicle downtime can you prevent?
issues.summary: Ashok Leyland opened an LCV dealership in Jagdalpur on 23 November 2026. The company reports four service bays, its fourth LCV dealership in Chhattisgarh and more than 945 LCV customer touchpoints nationwide. RPHV's lesson: measure vehicle downtime and the reasons for lost bay hours, not just workshop infrastructure.
issues.sourceNote: Ashok Leyland original release, 23 November 2026; inauguration and network snapshot as of that date, India. Counts are manufacturer-reported infrastructure, not vehicle transactions or independently audited utilisation.

metrics.label: Service bays
metrics.context: New Jagdalpur LCV facility

metrics.label: LCV dealership in Chhattisgarh
metrics.context: Company-reported state network

metrics.label: LCV customer touchpoints
metrics.context: Company-reported India network; not all workshops

issues.reportingType: OEM-reported facility inauguration and network snapshot; not monthly wholesales, customer registrations, survey data or measured workshop output.
intro: Ashok Leyland announced the opening of its light commercial vehicle dealership in Jagdalpur, Chhattisgarh, on 23 November 2026. Operated by Sri Hari Commercial, it combines sales, service and spare-parts functions and has four service bays.

The company identifies this as its fourth LCV dealership in Chhattisgarh and reports more than 945 LCV customer touchpoints across India. Touchpoints are not necessarily standalone workshops. Neither count measures repair volume or actual vehicle uptime.

RPHV interpretation: for a business vehicle, hours off the road can disrupt income. A bay is productive only when the job, technician, parts and authorisation are ready. Separate active repair time from waiting time before deciding to add capacity.

interpretation.heading: Measure the hours lost, not just the bays installed
points: Record arrival, diagnosis, approval, parts-ready, repair start, repair finish and release timestamps for each job.
Review waiting hours by cause: parts, approvals, technician availability, diagnosis or customer collection. Assign an owner to the largest controllable delay.
Schedule predictable maintenance around customer operating hours; do not promise a turnaround until capacity and parts are confirmed.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Capture the customer's operating schedule
desks.check: For commercial-vehicle deliveries, document route, usage, maintenance window and service contact.
desks.metric: Deliveries with documented operating and maintenance plan ÷ CV deliveries reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: A service appointment must fit the customer's actual working cycle.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Expose waiting time on each repair order
desks.check: Review closed ROs with arrival and ready-for-release timestamps; split elapsed time into active repair and waiting by reason.
desks.metric: Total arrival-to-ready hours ÷ closed ROs with complete timestamps (hours/RO)
desks.rationale: A bay count is not a measure of customer downtime.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Kit parts before planned maintenance
desks.check: Check tomorrow's booked jobs for VIN-correct parts, quantities and physical reservation.
desks.metric: Booked maintenance jobs with complete kits ÷ booked jobs requiring parts (%)
desks.rationale: Parts readiness prevents avoidable bay occupation.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Cost downtime risk in trade-ins
desks.check: For used commercial vehicles, document condition, likely reconditioning hours and approved cost before acquisition.
desks.metric: CV appraisals with approved repair-time and cost estimate ÷ CV appraisals reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: Unplanned refurbishment ties up capital and workshop capacity.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Identify approval-related delays
desks.check: Review open jobs awaiting credit, insurer or customer payment authorisation and record the responsible payer and next action.
desks.metric: Open ROs awaiting financial approval for more than 24 hours (count)
desks.rationale: Payment or credit uncertainty should not silently consume workshop capacity.

issues.huddleTitle: One delayed job. Five checks. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Choose a real delayed commercial-vehicle repair. Use the recorded timestamps to find the largest controllable delay and set a named owner, deadline and customer update.
huddle: 0–3 min: SALES confirms the customer's operating window and next commitment.
3–6 min: SERVICE traces arrival, diagnosis, repair and waiting timestamps.
6–9 min: SPARES verifies the parts kit and dated ETA for missing lines.
9–12 min: USED CARS checks whether refurbishment jobs compete for the same capacity.
12–15 min: ACCOUNTS checks payer approval; agree on the next action, owner, deadline and customer-update time.
limitations: The original manufacturer statement is dated 23 November 2026; the figures describe the new Jagdalpur facility and LCV network at announcement, not a monthly reporting period.

Four bays refers to this facility only; fourth dealership refers to Chhattisgarh only; more than 945 touchpoints refers to the nationwide Ashok Leyland LCV network, not an exact count or a count of workshops.
No measured bay utilisation, repair turnaround, investment, profitability, customer satisfaction or retail registration outcomes are supplied. No such improvement or comparison is claimed.
All operational checks and KPIs are RPHV recommendations. For percentage KPIs, a zero denominator is not applicable; report timestamp completeness alongside the service average.

issues.title: Five safety stars. Can the dealership explain what was actually tested?
issues.summary: Hyundai Motor India announced on 20 November 2026 that the updated Verna received five stars for both adult and child occupant protection under Bharat NCAP. The official assessment scores are 28.22/32 (adult) and 44/49 (child), from a July 2026 assessment. The finding applies to listed current-model variants, not automatically to every historical Verna. RPHV's lesson: convert rating headlines into accurate variant-specific customer advice and evidence-based safety repair practices.
issues.sourceNote: Original manufacturer press release published 20 November 2026; official Bharat NCAP 2026 fact sheet assessed July 2026, with no exact fact-sheet upload/publication day stated. India, Hyundai Verna 2026: 5-star adult and child ratings, adult 28.22 out of 32 and child 44.00 out of 49. Tested variants: 1.5 Turbo GDi DCT HX8 and 1.5 MPi iVT HX8; rating coverage restricted to 12 variants in official annexure. This is a standardized laboratory crash assessment, not a sales, registration, survey or real-road injury outcome dataset.

issues.reportingType: 2026 laboratory crash-assessment result for a specified India-market vehicle model; manufacturer announcement 20 November 2026 and official Bharat NCAP fact sheet assessed July 2026. These are assessment scores and stars, neither OEM-to-dealer domestic wholesales nor customer retail registrations, surveys, crash-frequency data or observed injury rates.
intro: Hyundai Motor India announced on 20 November 2026 that its updated Verna earned five stars for adult occupant protection and five stars for child occupant protection under Bharat NCAP. The official test-programme fact sheet records 28.22 points out of 32 for adult protection and 44.00 out of 49 for child protection.

The official assessment was conducted in July 2026. Bharat NCAP identifies the tested vehicles as the Verna 1.5 Turbo GDi DCT HX8 and 1.5 MPi iVT HX8; its annexure extends the rating to twelve listed current-model petrol variants. The rating must not be automatically attached to an earlier model-year Verna or an unlisted version.

The five-star summary does not mean perfect protection in every test or collision. The fact sheet reports marginal thigh protection in the frontal-offset test and specifies child-restraint arrangements used for child assessment. Safety features mentioned in the manufacturer's marketing may vary by trim; confirm the actual VIN and variant before promising equipment.

RPHV interpretation: customer trust improves when dealerships can explain both what the independent rating measures and what it cannot prove. Safe aftersales repair and transparent used-car appraisals are part of the same promise.

interpretation.heading: Turn a star badge into a verified customer promise
points: Train the sales team to show the official Bharat NCAP score sheet, identify the exact model/variant and explain the test conditions rather than presenting stars as a blanket safety guarantee.

Tie workshop inspection, any crash-related repair and replacement of safety systems to manufacturer-approved procedures and evidence; never declare a restraint or ADAS system safe without appropriate checks.
For used cars, distinguish tested 2026 variants from older models and reconcile repair history, safety equipment and ownership documents before using a rating in advertising.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Match the safety claim to the exact car
desks.check: For today's 2026 Verna enquiries, record variant/powertrain, verify that it appears in the official Bharat NCAP annexure, and explain adult and child scores without claiming accident-proof performance.
desks.metric: Enquiries with documented rating-applicability and score briefing ÷ sampled 2026 Verna enquiries (%)
desks.rationale: A five-star headline becomes misleading when applied to the wrong model year or promised as a universal outcome.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Document safety-critical repair verification
desks.check: Audit recent accident, windscreen, steering, restraint or driver-assistance repairs. Confirm prescribed inspection, calibration (where applicable), fault resolution and qualified quality sign-off before delivery.
desks.metric: Completed applicable safety-critical ROs with documented OEM-required verification ÷ applicable safety-critical ROs audited (%)
desks.rationale: Crash performance depends on systems being correctly repaired and returned to service.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Protect traceability of safety components
desks.check: For SRS/seatbelt/ADAS parts issued against an RO, verify VIN applicability, genuine sourcing, part-number supersession and traceable issue records; escalate substitutions.
desks.metric: Audited safety-part issue lines with verified VIN, approved source and traceability ÷ safety-part lines audited (%)
desks.rationale: An incorrect or untraceable safety-critical component can undermine repair quality.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Do not inherit a newer model's rating
desks.check: For every Verna or similar model in used stock, check model year/variant, repair history and warning-light or restraint-system evidence before citing any Bharat NCAP or Global NCAP rating.
desks.metric: Advertised used vehicles with verified rating applicability and safety-history evidence ÷ used vehicles carrying a safety-rating claim (%)
desks.rationale: Past model-year designs and different test protocols cannot automatically borrow the 2026 rating.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Keep safety repairs authorised and reconcilable
desks.check: Match each sampled accident/safety-system repair to itemised approved estimate, insurer/customer authorisation, parts invoices, labour and claim settlement status.
desks.metric: Safety-related repair invoices with complete approval and cost reconciliation ÷ sampled safety-related invoices (%)
desks.rationale: Safety-critical repairs should be properly authorised, costed and closed without ambiguous payer responsibility.

issues.huddleTitle: One rating enquiry. Five evidence checks. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Use a real recent 2026 Verna safety-related customer enquiry, or a documented analogous crash-rating question. This is a desk review, not a physical crash, SRS or ADAS test.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — SALES: verify model/variant against Bharat NCAP annexure and write a two-sentence accurate customer explanation.
Minutes 3–6 — SERVICE: show where OEM repair/check procedures and technician authorisation are recorded for safety-related work.
Minutes 6–9 — SPARES: validate VIN, approved source and traceability for one applicable safety part.
Minutes 9–12 — USED CARS: check whether an older listed car is incorrectly advertised using the new model's score.
Minutes 12–15 — ACCOUNTS: inspect one safety-repair invoice/claim for approvals and reconciled costs; record a Go / Hold / Correct decision, owner, deadline and customer-update time.
limitations: The Bharat NCAP fact sheet identifies July 2026 as the month and year of assessment, and 2026 as the publication year. Its exact release day is not stated in the fact sheet. Hyundai's own dated public announcement is 20 November 2026.
Adult 28.22/32 and child 44.00/49 are points in defined laboratory assessments, not a percentage of crash survival, future injury avoidance, survey ratings, registrations or customer transactions.

The two explicitly tested HX8 variants and the twelve variants covered by the official annexure must not be conflated. Do not transfer the assessment to past model-year Verna vehicles, other trims absent from the annexure or other NCAP protocols.

The official fact sheet's frontal-offset assessment shows marginal protection for the front occupants' thighs. A five-star aggregate is not a perfect result in every body region or every real-world crash.

Hyundai markets several driver-assistance and restraint features. Not every marketed feature is necessarily standard across the variant range; use a specific VIN/variant equipment sheet before stating availability. Airbag-count claims were deliberately excluded pending variant-level reconciliation.

No manufacturer domestic wholesale, FADA/VAHAN customer retail-registration figure, independent real-world crash outcome or dealership performance improvement is claimed. The five operational checks and KPI definitions are original RPHV recommendations.

issues.title: Battery repair capability moves east. Is your escalation process ready?
issues.summary: Porsche India announced a new Kolkata service centre on 17 November 2026, measuring more than 32,000 sq ft and equipped for high-voltage and battery repair. The company calls it its largest Indian aftersales facility and the only Eastern India facility able to undertake dedicated Porsche battery repairs. RPHV lesson: specialist equipment matters, but successful customer care also depends on safe triage, qualified ownership, parts availability, approvals and cost control.

Area exceeds 32,000 square feet. The Eastern India exclusivity statement applies only to dedicated Porsche battery repairs, is attributable to Porsche, and has not been independently audited. Not a monthly registrations, manufacturer-wholesale, transaction, survey or performance dataset.

issues.reportingType: Primary OEM corporate infrastructure announcement, dated 17 November 2026, about one facility in Kolkata, West Bengal, India. Figures describe area and manufacturer-stated service capabilities; no sales transactions, customer retail registrations, manufacturer domestic wholesales, dealer profitability, independent survey outcomes or measured throughput.
intro: On 17 November 2026, Porsche India announced the inauguration of its new Service Centre Kolkata, developed with dealer partner Bird Group. The manufacturer says the site covers more than 32,000 square feet and is its largest aftersales facility in India.

Porsche lists routine servicing, advanced diagnostics, mechanical work and dedicated structural and multi-material repair bays. It also reports a high-voltage work area and specialised battery-repair capability; the claim that it is the only dedicated Porsche battery-repair facility in Eastern India is a company statement, not an all-brand regional census.

RPHV interpretation: specialised repair facilities demonstrate where aftersales capability is heading. But a customer with a complex repair needs a dependable process long before equipment is used: accurate complaint capture, safe triage by authorised staff, clear referral, VIN-correct parts, repair approvals and a transparent payer decision.

interpretation.heading: Equipment is capacity. A controlled handoff creates confidence.
points: Map which repair categories can be safely done in-house, which require a manufacturer-authorised specialist and who communicates that decision to the customer.
Never promise an EV battery repair deadline or repairability before authorised diagnosis, parts availability and warranty eligibility are confirmed.
Track every referred vehicle or specialist repair through an owner, confirmed next update, authorised cost and documented return-to-customer quality check.

desks.rationale: Unconfirmed components can turn an expert diagnosis into an indefinite vehicle hold.

intro: PTI reported on 12 November 2026 that used-car retailer Spinny said it delivered 9,377 cars between 11 October and 10 November 2026, a 31-day festive window. The company described this as 39% higher than the corresponding 31-day festive period of 22 September–22 October 2025. Those are Spinny-attributed operational deliveries rather than registrations for India's total used-car market.

The company also reported SUVs representing 28% of its 2026 festive deliveries; media coverage says 21% in the earlier comparison window. A change in mix at one platform does not prove all Indian used-car consumers shifted at the same rate, nor does a reported delivery imply the relevant ownership-transfer record has already been updated.

RPHV interpretation: the more vehicles a dealership acquires or retails, the more important a disciplined deal file becomes. Each trade-in requires verified identity and title, independent inspection, an approved repair cost, truthful disclosure, a defined margin and documented transfer status. Otherwise an apparently successful exchange can become a capital, legal or customer-trust problem.

interpretation.heading: Volume is useful. Documented ownership and margin make it sustainable.
points: Do not use a platform's festive growth as an India-wide used-car market growth rate; record geography, channel, period and whether the reported number is deliveries or registrations.

Before accepting an exchange or re-listing a vehicle, verify RC identity, existing finance or hypothecation, lien/loan clearance, accident/repair history where available, and an authorised reconditioning budget.
Keep a register that separates sold-and-delivered vehicles from those whose ownership transfer is submitted, pending or verified complete; assign a named case owner and review ageing.

desks.name: SERVICE

desks.metric: Used-car refurbishments with approved inspection and repair scope ÷ used-car refurbishments started (%)
desks.rationale: Unapproved repairs erode resale margin and can leave undisclosed faults.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Price parts before committing margin
desks.check: For all planned reconditioning work, match VIN-correct parts, physical availability, price and supplier lead time to the job-cost sheet.
desks.metric: Reconditioning part lines with approved fitment, price and availability ÷ planned part lines (%)
desks.rationale: A missed cost or wrong part can turn a profitable bid into a loss.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Track title through confirmed transfer
desks.check: Audit vehicles acquired or retailed this week for verified RC/owner identity, hypothecation status, signed sale papers, transfer application evidence and documented final transfer outcome.
desks.metric: Sold used vehicles with verified completed ownership transfer ÷ sold vehicles due for completed transfer under their applicable process (%)
desks.rationale: Vehicle delivery and successful ownership-record transfer are not the same event.

desks.check: Reconcile purchase price, loan settlement, transport, repairs, taxes/fees, carrying cost and final customer receipts against each used-car stock number.
desks.metric: Used-car sales with approved fully reconciled contribution sheet ÷ used-car sales closed (%)
desks.rationale: Revenue is not net contribution until obligations and actual expenses are recognised.

RPHV's lesson for dealer groups is to approve staffing, service capability, parts supply and cash exposure before launch commitments become fixed costs.

intro: In a stock-exchange disclosure on 26 October 2026, Landmark Cars Limited enclosed a statement that it had received letters of intent from JSW Motors Limited for five passenger-car dealership outlets in Ahmedabad and Bhopal. Its stated plan covers two showrooms and one workshop in South Ahmedabad, and one showroom and one workshop in Bhopal.

The distinction matters: a letter of intent is a proposal-stage milestone, not evidence that these outlets are already operational. The release also describes JSW Motors as a separate brand from JSW MG Motor India. It says sales were expected in the next financial quarter, but supplies no confirmed launch date, expenditure budget, sales volume or dealer profitability forecast.

RPHV's operational lesson is to treat expansion as a stage-gated investment decision. Opening a location commits money, people, tooling and parts before demand or aftersales throughput is proven. Before declaring a centre 'ready', test whether all five functions can fulfill and reconcile the same customer promise.

interpretation.heading: An outlet count is not a business case
points: Translate each proposed site into a signed pre-opening readiness file: customer catchment, realistic order pipeline, facility schedule, technician competency and approved capital envelope.
Do not count a proposed showroom as delivered retail volume or a proposed workshop as usable service capacity. Use site-specific launch milestones and evidence.
Review cash burn, credit terms and parts exposure together. Escalate unresolved assumptions before committing to rent, inventory or headcount.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Test demand before fixing capacity
desks.check: For every proposed showroom, document its catchment, competing outlets, planned lead sources and a 90-day enquiry-to-delivery forecast with assumptions.
desks.metric: Proposed showrooms with signed 90-day demand forecasts / all proposed showrooms (%)
desks.rationale: A showroom location and a forecast are not proof of paid customer demand.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Prove workshop launch readiness
desks.check: For each proposed workshop, verify service-bay plan, trained technician coverage, safety procedures, diagnostic tools and escalation support; mark every gap.
desks.metric: Planned workshops passing a signed technician-and-tools readiness checklist / all planned workshops (%)
desks.rationale: An announced workshop cannot support customers without people, tools and safe processes.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Secure critical parts without overstocking
desks.check: Build a launch critical-parts list; verify OEM part numbers, order eligibility, supplier lead time and replenishment or return terms before initial stocking.
desks.metric: Critical launch part lines with verified number and supplier lead time / critical launch part lines reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: Cash held in launch stock is risky if fitment and supply assumptions are not validated.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Write down exchange exposure
desks.check: For the launch exchange policy, require an ownership check, inspection report, estimated reconditioning cost and authorised resale-margin floor on each appraisal.
desks.metric: Exchange appraisals with signed ownership, condition and margin sheets / all appraisals reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: An aggressive new-car acquisition strategy can conceal losses in the trade-in book.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Gate investment by cash runway
desks.check: Prepare a location-wise capital and operating budget including rental deposits, equipment, salaries, floorplan finance, working capital and downside break-even scenario.
desks.metric: Planned outlets with approved capex, monthly cash-runway and break-even sheets / total planned outlets (%)
desks.rationale: An LOI does not disclose investment requirements or establish that a new site will earn its cost of capital.

issues.huddleTitle: One proposed outlet. Five gates. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Use one actual proposed new outlet, or a live network expansion proposal if no new outlet is planned. Record evidence, one unresolved risk per desk, a named decision owner and deadline; a proposed site is not automatically launch-ready.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: show catchment evidence and the assumption behind the first 90-day demand forecast.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: verify technician, safe-equipment and bay-readiness gaps.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: test one critical item for fitment, order status and lead time.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: identify one exchange valuation or reconditioning margin risk.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: read out downside monthly cash need; record a Go / Hold / Rework decision, owner and deadline.
limitations: The original filing is dated 26 October 2026; this 20 November edition revisits that development for dealership planning. It is not an announcement of a new November transaction.
All 5 outlets, 3 showrooms and 2 workshops are proposed under letters of intent. No commissioning, actual deliveries, utilisation or financial return is verified in the source.
The filing mentions a prospective 'next financial quarter' for vehicle sales but offers no confirmed calendar launch date. Its forward-looking statement cautions that plans may change.

No capex, debt, projected sales, profitability or service volume is provided in the disclosure, so none is asserted. The five operational checks and denominator-defined metrics are RPHV recommendations.

intro: On 6 November 2026, the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) reported 5,07,768 passenger-vehicle retail registrations in October 2026. The same original data table shows 4,27,213 in September 2026 and 5,92,032 in October 2025: up 18.86% month-on-month, but down 14.23% year-on-year. These are customer retail registration records—not the vehicles manufacturers dispatch to dealers.

FADA also estimated passenger-vehicle dealer-channel inventory at roughly 43–45 days, unchanged from September. Inventory days are an association-level estimate, not the number of vehicles registered or a verified measure for every dealer. The release was compiled as of 4 November from 1,468 of 1,469 RTOs; 3W, CV and tractor registrations for Telangana were not available in the aggregate.

FADA attributes much of the annual decline to a shifted festive calendar: October 2025 contained both Navratri and Diwali, while Diwali fell in November 2026. That is the association's interpretation, not proof that every missed October purchase moved to November. RPHV's operating conclusion is narrower: after festive deliveries, reconcile each VIN's age, sale status, delivery paperwork and cash.

interpretation.heading: A market chart cannot replace a VIN-by-VIN stock and cash review
points: Read October's month-on-month and year-on-year registration changes together; do not describe the 14.23% annual fall alone as proof of demand collapse or the 18.86% monthly rise alone as sustained growth.

For a dealership, count unsold vehicles by days since inward receipt, separately from transit cars, invoiced-but-not-delivered units and customer-delivered vehicles. Define the denominator before calling anything 'stock days'.

Run a daily closure check across promised deliveries, PDI, accessories, registration, exchange and lender receipts; investigate any VIN that appears delivered but has an unresolved financial or documentation item.

desks.headline: Close the delivery pipeline by VIN
desks.check: Select all VINs promised for delivery in the next seven days and verify allocation, registration progress, finance clearance, PDI, accessories and the exact committed date.

desks.rationale: Industry registrations do not reveal whether a dealer's actual orders are ready to hand over.

desks.name: SERVICE

desks.check: Review all new vehicles held after pre-delivery inspection. Record defect, evidence, closure authority and promised customer-update time by VIN.
desks.metric: PDI-held VINs older than 48 hours (count)
desks.rationale: An invoiced vehicle with an unresolved defect is not a clean customer handover.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Clear accessory and fitment blockers
desks.check: For booked deliveries with pending accessories or fitments, check the correct part number, physical stock, fitting slot and supplier-confirmed ETA.
desks.metric: Booked deliveries with all promised parts ready ÷ booked deliveries requiring parts (%)
desks.rationale: Unavailable promised fitments can delay both customer delivery and final collection.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Do not lose margin in exchanges
desks.check: Before paying for a trade-in, verify RC, hypothecation, approved inspection, reconditioning estimate, resale assumptions and signed transfer documentation.
desks.metric: Exchange acquisitions with approved complete margin dossier ÷ total exchanges acquired (%)
desks.rationale: An unverified exchange can trap cash even while new-car retail is active.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Trace money against actual delivery
desks.check: Reconcile one week's delivered VINs with customer receipts, financing disbursements, booking advances, exchange adjustments and the final invoice.
desks.metric: Delivered VINs with unreconciled receipt or lender balance after 2 working days (count)
desks.rationale: Industry-level sales growth is not the same as money available in the dealer's bank.

huddle: Minutes 0–3 — SALES: confirm customer promise, VIN, finance and registration progress.
Minutes 3–6 — SERVICE: verify PDI release, open defects and signed quality clearance.
Minutes 6–9 — SPARES: verify all promised fitments, parts availability and dated ETA.
Minutes 9–12 — USED CARS: verify any linked exchange's title and margin sheet; otherwise record N/A.
Minutes 12–15 — ACCOUNTS: reconcile advance, lender balance and final invoice, then record Go/Hold, owner, deadline and customer update.
limitations: FADA release published 6 November 2026 reports October 2026 customer vehicle registrations; its underlying data were collated as of 4 November 2026 in collaboration with MoRTH and covered 1,468 of 1,469 RTOs. It is an as-of snapshot, not an immutable final census; late amendments could change numbers.

PV monthly comparisons are registration-based: 5,07,768 in October 2026 versus 4,27,213 in September 2026 and 5,92,032 in October 2025. The percentages have these distinct month-specific denominators. No assumption is made that RTO coverage is identical in all underlying months.

FADA notes that October 2026 vehicle registrations for the 3W, CV and tractor categories were unavailable for Telangana. Do not present the aggregate national total as complete in those classes; the feature is specifically PV.

FADA's roughly 43–45 PV inventory days is the association's dealer-channel estimate, not a VAHAN/RTO transaction value, independently audited stock take, or figure applicable to any particular dealership.

October's YoY fall is not interpreted as a proven demand collapse; FADA's festive-calendar explanation is plausible but cannot identify individual deferred purchases. November 2026 registration outcomes are not yet verified here.

SIAM manufacturer domestic sales/wholesales and FADA customer retail registration totals have different reporting definitions and scope; no direct arithmetic subtraction or dealer-inventory inference is made from the two series.

intro: On 30 March 2026, Maruti Suzuki announced 'Quickstop', a compact modified-container service facility designed for routine maintenance and minor repairs at places such as corporate campuses, airport zones and fleet hubs. The company identified 10 pilot facilities across Delhi-NCR, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Bagdogra, Calicut and Surat. Dealer partners operate the units while participating corporate entities or fleet operators provide the space.

On 15 June 2026, Maruti Suzuki separately introduced its Smart Maintenance Plan (SMP). Customers could select labour-only, parts-and-labour and other configurations; the company stated at least a 10% saving on labour under the plan, subject to terms. Published options extended up to 10 years/100,000 km for private vehicles, and up to 10 years/160,000 km for commercial vehicles. The plan is usable at authorised Maruti Suzuki dealer workshops across India.

Both releases describe propositions, not measured outcomes: neither source supplies a controlled comparison of repair turnaround, customer retention, number of prepaid-plan purchases or dealership operating margin. Their relevance to other dealers is as models to evaluate, not claims to copy verbatim.

interpretation.heading: The service promise needs an operating system
points: Choose a limited service menu and clearly separate on-site jobs from repairs requiring full workshop tools, diagnosis, safety controls or specialist technicians.
Offer an appointment only after checking location access, technician capacity, correct parts/consumables and a realistic return time; capture the customer's approval of extra work.
For prepaid packages, map covered and excluded items, eligibility, redemptions, workshop reimbursement and balances; measure economic outcomes before promising savings or scaling.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Explain service convenience without overpromising

desks.rationale: Convenience depends on a kept appointment and a safe handoff, not only proximity.

desks.rationale: A nearby service location still fails the customer if the correct consumables are missing.

intro: On 6 November 2026, Mahindra announced that its factory-fitted CNG XUV 3XO ZNG had received five stars under Bharat NCAP, with 29.36 out of 32 points for Adult Occupant Protection and 45 out of 49 for Child Occupant Protection. These are defined crash-assessment scores, not a prediction of protection in every real-world collision.

The full story is more specific than the showroom headline. The official Bharat NCAP XUV 3XO vehicle page says the original rating was published in November 2024 and was extended to the CNG family in November 2026. It also states that the revised child-protection score of 45/49 is applicable only to vehicles built from VIN MA1NS2NVPS2B98575 onwards; vehicles before that VIN retain 43/49. Both reported score sets correspond to five-star child ratings.

That production-cutoff note matters whenever a salesperson discusses a rating, a customer compares variants or a used-car appraiser assesses an earlier vehicle. The right sales promise identifies the exact vehicle and official rating applicability before quoting the headline.

interpretation.heading: Turn a safety badge into an evidence-backed explanation
points: Use the vehicle's actual VIN, fuel type, variant and manufacture record to check the official assessment's applicability; never assume every car sharing a model name carries exactly the same published score.

Explain standard airbags, electronic stability control, ISOFIX availability and the manufacturer's CNG gas-leak protection using approved documentation, without promising that any vehicle is injury-proof.
Record which safety information was communicated to the buyer, and refer technical or CNG-system questions to the authorised manufacturer procedure rather than ad-hoc workshop checks.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Verify the car behind the claim
desks.check: Before quoting a Bharat NCAP result, match actual VIN, variant and fuel system with the current official ratings-applicability notes; retain that check in the delivery file.
desks.metric: Safety-rating claims supported by VIN and variant check ÷ safety-rating claims made (%)
desks.rationale: The published assessment can contain production-batch exclusions that a generic model brochure does not show.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Complete a safety-focused handover
desks.check: Document OEM-prescribed pre-delivery warning-lamp checks and explain seat-belt, ISOFIX and relevant CNG safety instructions; escalate CNG faults to trained authorised staff.
desks.metric: Deliveries with signed safety/PDI handover checklist ÷ deliveries due (%)
desks.rationale: A high crash-test rating does not replace functioning safety equipment and owner understanding.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Do not guess on safety-critical parts
desks.check: Verify safety-system and CNG-related part numbers against the exact VIN and OEM catalogue before ordering or issuing replacement parts.
desks.metric: Safety-critical part orders with verified VIN fitment ÷ all safety-critical part orders (%)
desks.rationale: Correct part selection matters more than quick but incorrect substitution.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Check rating and modifications separately
desks.check: During acquisition, record VIN, fuel system as originally manufactured, known safety-system repairs and any non-OEM CNG modification; verify whether the tested rating actually applies.
desks.metric: Used-car appraisals with VIN-linked safety and fuel-system record ÷ total appraisals (%)
desks.rationale: A used vehicle's actual specification and repair history may differ from the car described in a sales advertisement.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Make safety charges transparent
desks.check: Match billed safety accessories or child-restraint equipment against approved quotations, actual fitment and customer acknowledgement; flag unsupported safety-related charges.
desks.metric: Deliveries with safety-accessory bill-to-fitment reconciliation ÷ deliveries containing such items (%)
desks.rationale: Trust requires accurate invoices as well as accurate vehicle information.

issues.huddleTitle: Check one VIN before making a five-star claim
issues.huddleSummary: Use one live quotation or incoming used car. Each desk checks one part of the evidence chain. Finish with the approved claim, a gap owner and a customer update.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: identify actual VIN, variant and fuel type; check the rating's applicability and cutoff note.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: verify PDI record, warning indicators, seat-belt/ISOFIX explanation and appropriate CNG safety instructions.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: confirm any safety-critical replacement item is matched to VIN and manufacturer catalogue.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: review manufacturing specification, repairs and modifications that affect what can accurately be promised.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: reconcile billed safety items with approved scope; record 'claim verified', 'hold' or 'correct communication', an owner and deadline.
limitations: The 6 November 2026 manufacturer statement and official Bharat NCAP vehicle page concern a defined model and assessment; the results are not retail registrations, factory wholesales, sales performance, accident statistics or guarantees in real-world collisions.

Mahindra's five-star announcement is company communication. Bharat NCAP's official vehicle listing independently confirms the original November 2024 assessment, November 2026 CNG extension and VIN-specific child-score note. It does not display the exact day of its November 2026 revision.

The Bharat NCAP listing notes that the CNG AX5 underwent a frontal offset test while side and pole results were carried over because the body structure and safety systems remain the same. Do not imply each variant underwent every test independently.

Older XUV 3XO vehicles before VIN MA1NS2NVPS2B98575 retain a 43/49 COP score; 45/49 applies from that VIN onward. This issue makes no blanket claim that every XUV 3XO ever built has a 45/49 COP score.
Mahindra's claim to be the first sub-compact CNG SUV with five stars is deliberately not repeated: sub-segment definitions and rival applicability would need additional independent checking.
These five dealership checks and ratios are RPHV editorial recommendations, not Bharat NCAP test criteria, OEM operational standards or a substitute for approved service and safety procedures.

For dealerships of any brand, an inspection checklist is useful only if the recorded findings are supported by evidence, the reconditioning estimate is fully costed and the sale contract tells the buyer what is and is not covered. A glossy sales listing cannot replace a traceable vehicle file.

interpretation.heading: Build the proof before the promise
points: A buyer should be able to trace the VIN, registration details, prior ownership, known condition, service history and inspection findings to the actual vehicle.

Treat digital listings and certification badges as invitations to inspect the evidence—not substitutes for the evidence itself.

desks.headline: Close the ownership evidence gap

intro: On 18 September 2026, Honda Cars India announced the ground-breaking of Phase II of its spare-parts warehouse at Doddaballapura near Bengaluru. The company said the planned addition would cover approximately 80,000 square metres with an investment of ₹450 crore. It projects 140,000 square metres of total site area after the expansion, including the 60,000-square-metre first phase operational since June 2025.

This is a useful example of investment in India's automotive aftersales supply chain, not evidence that service parts are arriving faster today. The stated hub serves the company's car, two-wheeler and power-products businesses. The release does not provide a completion date, order-fill rate, transit-time improvement or local-dealership result.

For managers, the actionable question is narrower: for each vehicle held up by a part, does someone know the correct part number, actual order status, dated supplier ETA, assigned owner and next customer update?

interpretation.heading: The last mile matters more than the headline
points: Separate stock at the central warehouse from stock available to your specific workshop; availability is not a promise until an order and delivery date are confirmed.
Make parts-blocked repair orders visible each morning. Record VIN, part number, supplier acknowledgement, ETA, escalation owner and customer update time.
Use scheduled repairs and actual fast-moving consumption to plan genuine demand. Avoid speculative buying that turns working capital into ageing inventory.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Protect accessory-ready deliveries
desks.check: For the next seven days' planned vehicle handovers, verify VIN-specific accessories and fitment slots before confirming the delivery time.
desks.metric: Deliveries with required accessories physically ready ÷ all deliveries requiring accessories (%)
desks.rationale: Do not equate a parts order with fitted accessories.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Keep parts-blocked ROs in sight
desks.check: Review every open repair order stopped by unavailable parts; confirm its age, revised promise and next customer-update owner.
desks.metric: Open parts-blocked ROs older than 48 hours (number)
desks.rationale: The customer needs a dependable next update even when the part is unavailable.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Know which ETA is confirmed
desks.check: Check the ten most urgent unfulfilled parts requests for VIN fitment, supplier acknowledgement, order status and a dated ETA.
desks.metric: Open parts orders with a supplier-confirmed ETA ÷ all open parts orders (%)
desks.rationale: An estimated arrival date without supplier acknowledgement is still a risk, not a delivery commitment.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Price reconditioning delays
desks.check: Before accepting an exchange vehicle, verify cost and availability of critical repair parts, including delayed or discontinued items.
desks.metric: Acquired used vehicles with parts-verified reconditioning sheets ÷ total acquired used vehicles (%)
desks.rationale: Low acquisition price cannot protect margin when essential parts are unavailable.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Unblock parts-related cash
desks.check: Match supplier advances and payments against purchase orders, invoices and goods received notes; flag amounts against unreceived items.
desks.metric: Unmatched parts-supplier advances older than 7 calendar days (₹)
desks.rationale: Paid does not mean received, and received does not mean correctly issued.

issues.huddleTitle: One missing part. Five decisions. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Choose one actual parts-blocked repair order and use five three-minute reviews to resolve availability, fitment, customer promise, reconditioning exposure and cash.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 | Service: Explain the blocked RO, promised date and last customer update.
Minutes 3–6 | Spares: Verify exact part, supplier order status and dated ETA; flag unconfirmed information.
Minutes 6–9 | Sales: Check whether the issue also affects a planned new-car or accessory delivery.
Minutes 9–12 | Used Cars: Check whether the same part could delay an exchange-vehicle reconditioning job.
Minutes 12–15 | Accounts: Confirm any advance exposure, assign owners and schedule next customer/management update.
limitations: The 18 September 2026 company release is a project announcement, not a report from 9 November 2026; the newsletter date is the publication date of RPHV commentary.
Phase II had only reached the announced ground-breaking stage. The cited ₹450 crore and 80,000 m² refer to planned investment and addition, not completed assets or verified expenditure.
The 140,000 m² is the company's projected combined facility area after Phase II; 60,000 m² Phase I was reported operational in June 2025.
The company release gives no actual fill-rate, repair turnaround, delivery lead-time, opening/completion date or proof of dealer-level improvement.
The source is specific to one supplier network; the five checks are brand-neutral RPHV recommendations, not company performance targets. No vehicle wholesale or retail registrations are reported.

issues.reportingType: India October 2026 retail registrations (RTO-based); FADA national passenger-vehicle channel inventory-day estimate; forward-looking FADA dealer survey. NOT factory wholesales or dealership audited financial data.
intro: FADA's 6 November report places October 2026 passenger-vehicle retail registrations at 5,07,768 and estimates channel inventory at around 43–45 days, unchanged from September. The registrations reflect vehicles recorded at RTOs; the inventory-day figure is an association-level stock estimate. These are different measures, and neither shows the cash available in a particular dealership.

Looking ahead, 51.65% of respondents to FADA's Online Members' Survey expected retail growth in November. That is sentiment, not a forecast guaranteed to come true. With Diwali on 8 November, the test for a dealer is whether scheduled handovers become completed, correctly accounted transactions.

A vehicle can have a customer invoice, a registration entry and a promised delivery without every supporting receipt, bank payout, exchange adjustment or credit note being reconciled. The useful festive-season control is a short, daily exception list: which unit is still in stock, who owes which amount and who owns the next action?

interpretation.heading: Turn festive activity into reconciled business
points: Separate three records in the daily review: OEM-to-dealer dispatches (wholesale), customer registrations (retail), and actual dealership receipts. Reconcile differences instead of treating them as interchangeable sales figures.
Age each unsold vehicle and record its landed cost and funding status; do not apply the nationwide 43–45-day estimate to any individual stock ledger.

Close the handover loop: finance disbursement, customer balance, exchange adjustment, accessory bill and delivery acknowledgement must be traceable to the same vehicle/VIN. Track unresolved items by owner and date.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Check each promised handover
desks.check: From today's delivery list, match VIN, customer invoice, registration status, lender approval and payment clearance before confirming handover.
desks.metric: Delivery files with verified clearance ÷ deliveries scheduled today (%)
desks.rationale: A delivery promise should be supported by a complete customer and payment record.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Close PDI exceptions before release
desks.check: For each vehicle marked ready for delivery, confirm signed pre-delivery inspection and closure or authorised escalation of any open defect.
desks.metric: Planned deliveries with signed, cleared PDI ÷ planned deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: A last-minute repair hold is easier to manage when visible to Sales and Accounts.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Match accessories to the invoice
desks.check: Review billed accessories on today's handover list and confirm fitment, issue records and approved exceptions with Sales.
desks.metric: Billed accessory lines without verified fitment or issue (count)
desks.rationale: A missing accessory can delay handover or create avoidable billing disputes.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Record the full exchange adjustment
desks.check: For each exchange attached to a new delivery, verify acquisition value, existing loan closure/no-dues status, ownership documents and ledger treatment.
desks.metric: Exchange-linked deliveries with approved settlement sheet ÷ exchange-linked deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: Unresolved loans and undocumented offsets make the sale harder to reconcile.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Trace the money vehicle by vehicle
desks.check: Match each delivered VIN to customer receipts, lender disbursement, exchange offsets, taxes and any OEM receivable; assign ageing and owner to mismatches.
desks.metric: Unreconciled delivery-linked balance aged over 2 working days (₹)
desks.rationale: Completed deliveries are not the same as fully settled or reconciled transactions.

issues.huddleTitle: One VIN. Five checks. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Select one live festive handover at risk. Spend three minutes with each desk, capture the gap and end with one named owner per unresolved item.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — SALES: Show the VIN, customer promise, invoice and payment/registration status.
Minutes 3–6 — SERVICE: Confirm signed PDI or identify the release blocker.
Minutes 6–9 — SPARES: Confirm accessories billed, issued and fitted.
Minutes 9–12 — USED CARS: If an exchange is involved, confirm loan settlement and adjustment documentation; otherwise record no exchange.
Minutes 12–15 — ACCOUNTS: Match bank receipts and lender payout to the VIN; assign owners and deadlines for every exception.
limitations: Original October 2026 FADA-hosted report/PDF was not accessible during research; the 6 November statement was checked through a separately hosted attributed reproduction and credible independent reports. The association's publicly visible LinkedIn feed corroborates the 43–45-day stock statement and 51.65% November sentiment, but exact first-party PDF footnotes remain unchecked. Do not publish until reconciled.
FADA's ~43–45 inventory days describe the passenger-vehicle channel at an industry level, not an audited figure for an individual dealership or a rupee financing cost.

51.65% is the share of respondents to a FADA Online Members' Survey expecting growth in November 2026. Survey sample size, response rate and full questionnaire were not verified; it is not a measure of realised sales or a probability.

October 2026 retail registrations are not manufacturer-to-dealer dispatches (wholesales). The festive calendar differs from October 2025 because Diwali is in November 2026; simple annual comparisons can mislead.
The recommended checks and two-working-day exception threshold are RPHV editorial management suggestions, not FADA, OEM, RBI or statutory norms.

issues.reportingType: FADA-reported retail registrations for 1–31 October 2026; not manufacturer wholesales, workshop inflow, or a dealer-level survey
intro: The number worth noticing is not a workshop target. FADA's 6 November 2026 statement says electric-vehicle retail registrations reached approximately 3.55 lakh across vehicle categories in October 2026. Within passenger vehicles, electric models represented 7.30% of 5,07,768 retail registrations. These are two different denominators.

A registered vehicle is not a service visit. It would be misleading to turn a month's EV retail data into a forecast for service revenue, trained-technician demand or diagnostic failures. But the changing mix is a useful reason to audit how enquiries and repair orders are received, identified and handed to the right people.

For the next EV or hybrid customer, can the advisor capture the exact vehicle and complaint, can the workshop assign work only within its training and equipment limits, and can the customer get a realistic update? That is the operational test, not a slogan about electrification.

interpretation.heading: Prepare the service process before the next exception
points: Identify the powertrain and exact vehicle/VIN at appointment and job-card creation; do not treat EV, hybrid and conventional vehicles as interchangeable.

For work involving high-voltage systems, follow the manufacturer procedure and route only to authorised, appropriately trained personnel; escalate otherwise. This is a safety and process recommendation, not a claim about an industry-wide skills gap.
Agree on parts availability, diagnostic authorisation, expected completion and next customer-update time before making a delivery promise.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Explain ownership support at handover
desks.check: For each EV delivery, verify that the customer receives model-specific charging, roadside assistance, warranty and service-booking guidance.
desks.metric: EV deliveries with recorded customer orientation ÷ EV deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: A useful handover reduces avoidable confusion over whom to contact for help.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Route the job to the right technician
desks.check: Review electrified-vehicle job cards for VIN/powertrain identification, a named trained owner and safe escalation where high-voltage competence or equipment is unavailable.
desks.metric: EV/hybrid ROs with documented qualified assignment and triage ÷ EV/hybrid ROs (%)
desks.rationale: Good routing protects safety and reduces unowned diagnostic delays.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Confirm fitment before quoting
desks.check: For an electrified-vehicle parts request, match VIN and part number and record availability, supersession and supplier ETA before promising completion.
desks.metric: EV/hybrid parts requests with verified VIN and ETA ÷ EV/hybrid parts requests (%)
desks.rationale: A wrong or delayed component can keep a specialist bay occupied.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Document battery and warranty evidence
desks.check: Before acquiring a used EV, record the VIN, warranty eligibility, charging accessories and an OEM-supported battery assessment where available.
desks.metric: Used EV appraisals with battery/warranty evidence ÷ used EV appraisals (%)
desks.rationale: Unknown battery or warranty status makes an appraisal unnecessarily speculative.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Track outstanding electrified-vehicle claims
desks.check: Review EV/hybrid warranty claims for complete invoices, approvals, labour documentation and payment status; assign owners to overdue cases.
desks.metric: Value of EV/hybrid warranty claims outstanding over 30 days (₹)
desks.rationale: Correct technical work still needs timely claim documentation and reconciliation.

issues.huddleTitle: One electrified-vehicle case. Five clean handoffs.
issues.huddleSummary: Use one real EV or hybrid case; if none is currently open, use the latest genuine customer enquiry. Record an owner, the next step and a deadline; never perform high-voltage work as part of the huddle.
huddle: Minutes 0–3: Sales checks what ownership, warranty and service guidance the customer received.
Minutes 3–6: Service confirms VIN, complaint, trained assignment and any safety/escalation limit.
Minutes 6–9: Spares validates any requested part number, fitment and availability.
Minutes 9–12: Used Cars checks what evidence would be needed if this vehicle came in for exchange.
Minutes 12–15: Accounts checks claim/billing documentation and the team records one owner, deadline and customer update.
limitations: FADA's statement, dated 6 November 2026, concerns October 1–31 retail registrations. No November registrations, future sales or aftersales RO volumes are inferred.
The approximately 3.55 lakh EV figure covers all vehicle categories. The 7.30% EV figure is a share of PASSENGER-VEHICLE retail registrations; the percentages are not interchangeable.

The October release was not available as a directly inspected PDF on the FADA domain (site access blocked); its FADA-authored statement was checked in a syndicated reproduction and its major figures corroborated by independent dated trade coverage. Original publisher-hosted document and RTO scope/coverage footnotes remain unverified; retain an approval hold.
Monthly retail-registration figures are not manufacturer wholesale dispatches, billings, cash collections, service visits, repair demand or evidence of staff competency gaps.
FADA attributes the October 2026 year-on-year comparison to the unusual festival calendar; this issue does not infer a measured service-workload effect.

All five desk checks and suggested metrics are original RPHV guidance, not FADA standards or mandatory manufacturer service procedures. Follow the applicable OEM safety directions; do not attempt high-voltage work without appropriate training/authorisation.
If no relevant EV/hybrid cases occurred, record the metric as not applicable, not 100%.

issues.summary: FADA's provisional Navratri passenger-vehicle registrations were 10.39% higher than in 2024 but 21.91% lower than in 2025. The two comparisons use different festival windows. Before revising targets, separate calendar effects from the dealership's actual enquiry-to-delivery performance.

issues.reportingType: Provisional customer vehicle registrations (FADA/MoRTH); not manufacturer wholesales, dealer invoicing, or a representative enquiry survey
intro: The headline depends on the comparison chosen. In its 21 October release, FADA recorded 1,82,728 passenger-vehicle registrations during Navratri 2026 (11-20 October). That was 10.39% above the 1,65,534 registrations recorded across the ten-day 2024 Navratri period, yet 21.91% below the 2,34,004 recorded during Navratri 2025.

The 2025 festival window ran for eleven days (22 September-2 October), compared with ten days in 2026 and 2024. FADA also identified the September 2025 GST changes and accumulated demand as factors that made last year's base unusual. The reported decline should therefore not be treated as a clean measure of weakened customer interest.

For a dealership, the more useful question is operational: Of customers promising a festive delivery, how many cars are allocated, finance-cleared, registered and actually ready to hand over? Review that chain before changing discounts, staffing or purchase decisions. Registrations reflect retail activity; OEM dispatches are a different data series.

interpretation.heading: Read the market. Then inspect your own funnel.
points: Compare matched days or clearly label uneven festival windows; also examine the same dealership's week-by-week enquiry, booking and delivery stages.
For the coming seven days, verify every promised delivery against vehicle allocation, finance status, registration and required fitments. A booking is not a confirmed handover.
Record why each deferred delivery slipped: customer request, allocation, documents, finance, PDI or accessories. The reason tells managers which process to improve.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Check the promised delivery, not just the booking
desks.check: For all deliveries promised within seven days, confirm the customer's date, available VIN, finance approval and registration progress.
desks.metric: Fully confirmed deliveries ÷ deliveries promised in next 7 days (%)
desks.rationale: This identifies promises at risk without confusing industry registrations with your own sales funnel.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Release cars only after PDI closure
desks.check: Match every planned handover VIN to a completed pre-delivery inspection and closure of any safety or functional defects.
desks.metric: Deliveries with completed, signed PDI ÷ total deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: An incomplete inspection can turn a festive delivery into an early complaint.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Flag accessories holding up handovers
desks.check: Review accessories and fitments promised for the next seven days; verify kit availability, technician slot and supplier ETA.
desks.metric: Deliveries with all promised accessories ready before handover ÷ deliveries requiring accessories (%)
desks.rationale: Missing fitments create preventable delays and broken customer commitments.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Close exchange appraisals before the delivery date
desks.check: Identify upcoming deliveries with exchange commitments; confirm physical appraisal, ownership paperwork and approved trade-in value.
desks.metric: Exchange-linked deliveries with signed-off appraisals ÷ exchange-linked deliveries due (%)
desks.rationale: Unresolved exchange values can prevent a confirmed new-vehicle handover.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Clear money and documents before release
desks.check: Reconcile advances, lender payout confirmation, invoice balance and statutory charges on each delivery-due file.
desks.metric: Scheduled deliveries fully payment-cleared before handover ÷ scheduled deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: A delivery is operationally complete only when financial and documentation controls are clear.

issues.huddleTitle: Five desks. One delivery at risk. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Use one real delivery file to identify the single blocker that could disappoint the customer, then assign its owner and deadline.
huddle: Minutes 0-3: Sales checks customer commitment, allocation and confirmed date.
Minutes 3-6: Service validates the VIN's PDI and any open defect.
Minutes 6-9: Spares confirms accessories, fitment slot and any part ETA.
Minutes 9-12: Used Cars clears exchange valuation and transfer paperwork, if applicable.
Minutes 12-15: Accounts confirms payment and registration-related clearance; record the owner and customer update time.
limitations: FADA's 21 October report was provisional. Retail data were collated as of 21 October 2026 from 1,468 of 1,469 RTOs in collaboration with MoRTH; figures can change with late registrations or revisions.

The festival windows differ: 2026 (11-20 Oct, 10 days), 2025 (22 Sep-2 Oct, 11 days), 2024 (3-12 Oct, 10 days). The -21.91% 2025 comparison is not a like-for-like daily or calendar-month growth measure.

FADA notes that Telangana registration data for 3W, CV and tractor categories were unavailable for Navratri 2026; this caveat applies to relevant all-vehicle totals, though PV is not listed among the missing categories.

FADA's discussion of GST-linked pent-up demand is industry interpretation, not causal proof about every dealership. Festival registrations cannot establish dealership enquiry conversion or profitability.

This article contains no October 2026 full-month FADA retail figure. It does not combine festival retail registrations with October manufacturer wholesale dispatches as if they describe the same period.
The five practical checks, metrics and 15-minute huddle are original RPHV operational suggestions, not FADA or OEM performance standards.
